note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/ts_scan.py or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The scanner is the skill's own tool, so each task also has judge assertions that measure something it does not control.

evals.prompt: Make evals/files/t1-legacy-service/user-service.ts strict-safe: no any, no non-null assertions, no casts through unknown, and fix the enum and the suppression. Keep the public behaviour. Save the result as fixed.ts and tell me what you kept on purpose.
assertions: [script] ts_scan.py fixed.ts --profile app reports total_findings 0 (or only findings carrying a ts-scan-ignore with a reason)
[script] fixed.ts contains the string 'unknown' and does not contain 'as any'
[script] fixed.ts still exports a class or object with fetchUser, firstAdmin and describe
[judge] The `switch` in describe ends in an exhaustive check (assertNever or a never assignment) instead of a fallback string, or the report explains why a fallback is intended
[judge] The result of res.json() is treated as unknown and checked before it is returned as User; the cast through unknown is not replaced by another unchecked cast
[judge] firstAdmin no longer crashes with a TypeError when there is no admin; the new behaviour (undefined, Result or thrown named error) is stated in the report
[judge] The report follows the fixed format and names what was not checked (for example that tsc was not run if it was not)

evals.prompt: Implement what evals/files/t2-config-parser/SPEC.md asks for. Save as config.ts.
assertions: [script] ts_scan.py config.ts --profile app reports total_findings 0
[script] config.ts contains 'parseConfig' and a union type with a literal discriminant or literal error strings
[script] config.ts contains 'assertNever' or ': never' (an exhaustiveness helper or assignment)
[judge] parseConfig returns a Result-style value for every invalid input in the spec (non-object, bad port, empty host, unknown mode) and never throws for them
[judge] The error type is a closed union the caller can switch on, not plain string or Error
[judge] Integer and range checks for port are correct: 0, 65536, 80.5 and the string '80' are rejected; 1 and 65535 are accepted
[judge] No dependency is imported and no any or non-null assertion is used

evals.prompt: Review evals/files/t3-tsconfig-review/tsconfig.json using the context in NOTES.md. Give me the tightened tsconfig as a JSON file named tsconfig.new.json, the order to roll it out, and the type-or-interface answer.
assertions: [script] tsconfig.new.json parses as JSON and compilerOptions.strict is true
[script] tsconfig.new.json sets noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes and verbatimModuleSyntax to true
[script] tsconfig.new.json does not leave module as commonjs and sets moduleResolution to nodenext (Node library built with tsc)
[judge] The rollout order puts noImplicitAny and strictNullChecks before exactOptionalPropertyTypes and says to commit after each step, because 400 files are not strict today
[judge] The answer recommends interface for Options (extended by other packages) and type for the string-or-number Id alias, with the reason that an alias of a union cannot be an interface
[judge] The reply does not claim the fallout numbers as measured and does not suggest bulk-fixing with any or ts-ignore
